scenes.title: $1.29 trillion in card debt
scenes.sub: A new record for U.S. credit card balances
scenes.sub_html: A new record for U.S. credit card balances

lines.say: Americans now owe one point two nine trillion dollars on credit cards. That's a record.
lines.show: Americans now owe $1.29 trillion on credit cards. That's a record.

lines.say: Here's the full debt picture, and what it means for you.
lines.show: Here's the full debt picture, and what it means for you.

lines.say: Total household debt hit nineteen point one trillion, up three hundred thirty four billion in three months.
lines.show: Total household debt hit $19.1 trillion, up $334 billion in three months.

lines.say: Most of it is mortgages. Then auto loans, student loans and credit cards.
lines.show: Most of it is mortgages. Then auto loans, student loans and credit cards.

lines.say: Five percent of all that debt is now behind on payments.
lines.show: 5% of all that debt is now behind on payments.

lines.say: And card debt is the expensive kind. The average card charging interest was at twenty two point three six percent.
lines.show: And card debt is the expensive kind. The average card charging interest was at 22.36%.

lines.say: The fix: pay your full statement balance each month, and you generally pay no interest on purchases.
lines.show: The fix: pay your full statement balance each month, and you generally pay no interest on purchases.

lines.say: Can't? Pay as far above the minimum as you can.
lines.show: Can't? Pay as far above the minimum as you can.

scenes.takeaway: The cheapest debt is the debt you never carry.
scenes.source: Data: New York Fed (Nov. 10, 2026); Federal Reserve G.19
